marking_schemes.scheme_text: D or Sodium Hydroxide or NaOH
key_points: Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is a strong electrolyte that completely dissociates into ions in solution
Alcohol and sucrose are non-electrolytes; carbonic acid is a weak electrolyte (partial dissociation)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The correct answer is D — Sodium hydroxide (NaOH). It is a strong electrolyte and completely dissociates into Na+ and OH- ions when dissolved in water. Alcohol and sucrose do not dissociate at all, and carbonic acid only partially dissociates.
common_errors: Some candidates selected carbonic acid instead of sodium hydroxide
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach the concept of complete ionization and partial ionization with examples to give a thorough understanding of strong and weak electrolytes.

key_points: Chlorine is the most electronegative among the elements listed (Mg, Cl, Al, S)
Electronegativity increases across a period; Cl (Period 3, Group 17) has the highest electronegativity among the options
marking_schemes.model_answer: The correct answer is B — Chlorine. Among the given elements, chlorine has the highest electronegativity because it is in Period 3 furthest to the right (Group 17) and has the greatest tendency to attract electrons toward itself.
common_errors: A few candidates chose sulphur over chlorine
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the trends in the properties of elements across a period/group with reference to the variation in electronic configuration.

key_points: The reason aluminium is used in the alloy duralumin is that it brings lightness (low density)
Duralumin is used in aircraft construction where low weight is essential
marking_schemes.model_answer: The correct answer is C — Aluminium brings lightness. Aluminium's low density makes duralumin lightweight, which is essential for applications such as aircraft bodies.
common_errors: A few candidates made the error of selecting 'Aluminium is brittle'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Familiarise students with the role of each metal used in an alloy.

key_points: Concentrated sulphuric acid (H2SO4) is used to dry HCl gas
It is suitable because it does not react with HCl gas and is a drying agent
CaO, ZnO, and Al2O3 are basic drying agents and would react with the acidic HCl gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: The correct answer is A — Concentrated H2SO4. It is used to dry HCl gas because it is an acidic drying agent that does not react with HCl. Basic drying agents such as CaO would react with the acidic gas.
common_errors: A few candidates confused the drying agent of ammonia and HCl gas and selected CaO instead of concentrated H2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the meaning of the terms with relevant examples.

key_points: Methane (CH4) is the hydrocarbon that is a greenhouse gas
Methane is produced by decomposition of organic matter and contributes significantly to the greenhouse effect
marking_schemes.model_answer: The correct answer is D — Methane (CH4). Methane is a significant greenhouse gas, contributing to global warming by trapping heat in the atmosphere.
common_errors: Some candidates chose ethane over methane
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make students aware of the impact of various gases on our environment.

key_points: Conversion of ethanol to ethene by concentrated sulphuric acid is dehydration
Concentrated H2SO4 removes a water molecule (chemically combined H2O) from ethanol
marking_schemes.model_answer: The correct answer is dehydration. When concentrated sulphuric acid acts on ethanol, it removes a molecule of water to produce ethene, which is a dehydration reaction: C2H5OH → C2H4 + H2O.
common_errors: Several candidates were confused between dehydration and dehydrogenation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise on the variation of products when temperature conditions change.

key_points: When sodium chloride is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid below 200°C, sodium hydrogen sulphate (NaHSO4) is formed along with HCl gas
At higher temperature (above 200°C), sodium sulphate (Na2SO4) is formed instead
marking_schemes.model_answer: When sodium chloride is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid below 200°C, one of the products formed is sodium hydrogen sulphate (NaHSO4): NaCl + H2SO4(conc.) → NaHSO4 + HCl.
common_errors: Many candidates wrote chlorine instead of sodium hydrogen sulphate
Some missed the third word 'sulphate' in the name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise on the variation of products when temperature conditions change.

key_points: When ammonia reacts with excess chlorine, nitrogen trichloride (NCl3) is formed
When ammonia is in excess over chlorine, ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) and nitrogen are formed instead
marking_schemes.model_answer: When ammonia reacts with excess chlorine, nitrogen trichloride (NCl3) is formed: NH3 + 3Cl2(excess) → NCl3 + 3HCl.
common_errors: A large number of candidates did not select the correct option (nitrogen trichloride)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the logic behind the products formed in the reaction between ammonia and chlorine with the varying conditions, as to which one is in excess.

key_points: Substitution reactions are characteristic reactions of alkanes
Alkenes and alkynes undergo addition reactions; alkanes undergo substitution (e.g. halogenation)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Substitution reactions are characteristic reactions of alkanes. In the presence of UV light, alkanes undergo halogenation by substitution, whereas alkenes and alkynes prefer addition reactions.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote alkenes instead of alkanes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of saturation and unsaturation to give students the understanding of the type of reaction (addition or substitution) that a particular organic substance would undergo.

key_points: In Period 3, sodium (Na) is the most metallic element
Metallic character decreases across a period from left to right; Na is the leftmost metal in Period 3
marking_schemes.model_answer: In Period 3, sodium (Na) is the most metallic element. Metallic character decreases across a period from left to right, and sodium, being in Group 1 (the leftmost), is the most metallic.
common_errors: Almost all candidates attempted this subpart correctly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the trends in the properties of elements across a period/group with reference to the variation in electronic configuration.

key_points: Copper(II) oxide is reduced by hydrogen gas to form copper metal and water
Balanced equation: CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: The balanced chemical equation for the reduction of copper(II) oxide by hydrogen is: CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O. Hydrogen acts as the reducing agent.
common_errors: A few candidates wrote CuO2 for copper(II) oxide instead of CuO
Some wrote 2H instead of H2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

key_points: Sodium hydroxide reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to form sodium sulphate and water
Balanced equation: 2NaOH + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + 2H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: The balanced equation for the action of dilute sulphuric acid on sodium hydroxide is: 2NaOH + H2SO4 → Na2SO4 + 2H2O.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the formula of the product as NaSO4 instead of Na2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

key_points: Zinc sulphide reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to form zinc sulphate and hydrogen sulphide gas
Balanced equation: ZnS + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2S↑
marking_schemes.model_answer: The balanced equation for the action of dilute sulphuric acid on zinc sulphide is: ZnS + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2S↑. Hydrogen sulphide gas is evolved.
common_errors: Several candidates represented zinc sulphide incorrectly as ZnSO3 or ZnSO4
Some carelessly used HCl instead of H2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

key_points: Ammonium hydroxide added to ferrous sulphate produces ammonium sulphate and ferrous hydroxide precipitate
Balanced equation: FeSO4 + 2NH4OH → (NH4)2SO4 + Fe(OH)2
marking_schemes.model_answer: When ammonium hydroxide is added to ferrous sulphate solution: FeSO4 + 2NH4OH → (NH4)2SO4 + Fe(OH)2. A dirty green precipitate of iron(II) hydroxide is formed.
common_errors: A large number of candidates made errors in writing the formula of ammonium sulphate or ferrous sulphate
In several cases the equation was not balanced
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: H2C=CH2 + Cl2 → H2C(Cl)-CH2(Cl) or C2H4 + Cl2 → C2H4Cl2
key_points: Chlorine gas adds across the double bond of ethene in an addition reaction
Product: 1,2-dichloroethane (C2H4Cl2)
Balanced equation: C2H4 + Cl2 → C2H4Cl2
marking_schemes.model_answer: Chlorine gas reacts with ethene by addition across the double bond: C2H4 + Cl2 → C2H4Cl2 (1,2-dichloroethane).
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the product as C2H2Cl2 instead of C2H4Cl2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the concept of saturation and unsaturation to give students the understanding of the type of reaction (addition or substitution) that a particular organic substance would undergo.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Reddish brown or brown gas of nitrogen dioxide is formed.
key_points: Concentrated nitric acid oxidises sulphur to sulphuric acid
The observation is the evolution of reddish-brown/brown nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gas
S + 6HNO3(conc.) → H2SO4 + 6NO2 + 2H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: When concentrated nitric acid reacts with sulphur, a reddish-brown gas (nitrogen dioxide, NO2) is evolved.
accepted_alternatives: Brown gas of nitrogen dioxide is formed
common_errors: Many candidates wrote the equation or named the product instead of stating the observation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to read the questions carefully, answer specifically, with reference to what has been asked.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: The black copper (II) oxide turns into a pink or reddish-brown substance.
key_points: Ammonia reduces heated copper(II) oxide to copper metal
The black CuO turns into a pink/reddish-brown substance (copper metal)
2NH3 + 3CuO → N2 + 3Cu + 3H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: When ammonia gas is passed over heated copper(II) oxide, the black copper(II) oxide is reduced and turns into a pink or reddish-brown substance (copper metal).
common_errors: Several candidates incorrectly wrote the colour of copper as red or reddish or brown (imprecise)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Supplement theory adequately with practical work. Instruct students to record observations.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: The colour of the electrolyte remains blue / anode diminishes in size or becomes thinner / cathode becomes thicker.
key_points: When copper sulphate solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes, the anode dissolves (becomes thinner)
The cathode is deposited with copper (becomes thicker)
The blue colour of the electrolyte (copper sulphate solution) remains unchanged
marking_schemes.model_answer: When copper sulphate solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes, the anode gradually dissolves and becomes thinner while the cathode becomes thicker. The blue colour of the copper sulphate solution remains unchanged.
accepted_alternatives: Anode diminishes in size or becomes thinner
common_errors: Some common incorrect responses: cathode diminishes in size; blue colour of copper sulphate fades
In a few cases the change was noted without mention of the electrode
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Supplement theory adequately with practical work. Instruct students to record observations. Never disregard the importance of practical work.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Brisk effervescence / A gas given out extinguishes burning splinter and itself burns with pop sound.
key_points: Zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas
Observation: brisk effervescence is observed
The gas evolved (hydrogen) extinguishes a burning splint and itself burns with a pop sound
marking_schemes.model_answer: When a small piece of zinc is added to dilute hydrochloric acid, brisk effervescence is observed. The gas evolved (hydrogen) extinguishes a burning splint and itself burns with a pop sound.
accepted_alternatives: Brisk effervescence; gas burns with pop sound
common_errors: Instead of stating the test for the gas evolved, many candidates simply identified it as H2
Some stated the gas burns with a blue flame instead of stating that a burning splint is extinguished with a pop sound
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Supplement theory adequately with practical work. Instruct students to record observations.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: A decrepitating sound is heard / A reddish brown gas is given out / A yellow residue is left behind.
key_points: On strongly heating lead nitrate, a decrepitating (crackling) sound is heard
Reddish-brown nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gas is evolved
A yellow residue of lead monoxide (PbO) is left behind
marking_schemes.model_answer: When lead nitrate is heated strongly in a test tube: a decrepitating (crackling) sound is heard, reddish-brown nitrogen dioxide gas is evolved, and a yellow residue of lead monoxide is left behind.
accepted_alternatives: A reddish-brown gas is given out
A yellow residue is left behind
common_errors: Products formed were listed by many candidates without any noticeable observations
Some candidates wrote 'yellow precipitate of PbO is obtained' instead of 'yellow residue'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Supplement theory adequately with practical work. Instruct students to record observations.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Number of moles in 12 g of oxygen gas = 12/32 = 0.375 moles
key_points: Molecular mass of O2 = 2 × 16 = 32 g/mol
Number of moles = mass / molar mass = 12/32 = 0.375 moles
marking_schemes.model_answer: The molecular mass of oxygen gas (O2) = 2 × 16 = 32 g/mol. Number of moles in 12 g of O2 = 12/32 = 0.375 moles.
common_errors: Many candidates took the mass of one mole of oxygen gas as 16 instead of 32 (confusing atomic mass with molecular mass)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure students have clarity regarding molecules, moles, and molecular weight. Acquaint students with the following terms: number of moles, Avogadro's numbers of atoms/molecules, Relative atomic mass (RAM), Relative molecular mass (RMM), molar mass, molar volume, etc.

key_points: Mass of one atom of C = 12 / (6 × 10^23) g
common_errors: Calculations for weight of 10^22 atoms of carbon were incorrect in a number of cases, indicating inadequate understanding of the mole concept
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure students have clarity regarding molecules, moles, and molecular weight.

key_points: Molecular formula C6H18O3: divide each subscript by the HCF (3)
Empirical formula: C2H6O
marking_schemes.model_answer: To find the empirical formula of C6H18O3, divide each subscript by the highest common factor (HCF = 3): C: 6/3 = 2, H: 18/3 = 6, O: 3/3 = 1. The empirical formula is C2H6O.
common_errors: Many candidates attempted well but carried out elaborate calculations using percentage composition instead of simply reducing the molecular formula to its simplest ratio
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Drill in the minds of the students that the empirical formula can be obtained from the molecular formula by reducing it to the simplest ratio.

key_points: Structure H-C(H2)-C≡C-H is propyne (3 carbon atoms, triple bond)
IUPAC name: propyne (prop = 3 carbons, yne = triple bond)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The IUPAC name of the structure H-CH2-C≡CH (3 carbons with a triple bond) is propyne.
common_errors: Some candidates were confused between 'yne' and 'ene', giving propene instead of propyne
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Point out to students that the carbon atom C with the double or triple bond or functional group must be expressed in the lowest number.

key_points: Structure H-C(H2)-C(=O)-H is ethanal (acetaldehyde)
IUPAC name: ethanal (eth = 2 carbons, al = aldehyde functional group)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The IUPAC name of the structure H-CH2-CHO (2 carbons with an aldehyde group) is ethanal.
common_errors: Many candidates wrote 'ethanol' (alcohol) instead of 'ethanal' (aldehyde)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Stress on the difference between structural formula of alcohol and that of aldehyde. Give practice for greater clarity.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Triple bond between 2 carbon atoms / H – C ≡ C – H
key_points: The special feature of the structure of ethyne is the presence of a triple covalent bond between the two carbon atoms
Structure: H-C≡C-H
marking_schemes.model_answer: The special feature of the structure of ethyne is the presence of a triple covalent bond (≡) between the two carbon atoms: H–C≡C–H.
accepted_alternatives: Triple covalent bond between 2 C atoms
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned linear planar structure or three covalent bonds rather than specifying a triple covalent bond
Some gave incorrect answers such as 'unsaturated compound' or 'undergoes addition reaction'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise on the differences between saturated and unsaturated compounds — saturated have all single bonds and unsaturated ones either have double or triple bonds.

key_points: The saturated hydrocarbon containing two carbon atoms is ethane (C2H6)
Ethane belongs to the alkane series (CnH2n+2): 2 carbons → C2H6
marking_schemes.model_answer: The saturated hydrocarbon containing two carbon atoms is ethane (C2H6). It has only single C-C and C-H bonds.
common_errors: Some candidates stated ethene or ethyne instead of ethane
A few candidates gave the general name of the homologous series instead of the specific compound name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Emphasise on the differences between saturated and unsaturated compounds.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Structural formula of acetic acid: H-C(H2)-C(=O)-OH
key_points: Acetic acid (ethanoic acid) structural formula: CH3-COOH
Shows methyl group connected to carboxylic acid group: H3C-C(=O)-OH
marking_schemes.model_answer: The structural formula of acetic acid (ethanoic acid) is H3C-C(=O)-OH, where a methyl group (CH3) is attached to a carboxylic acid group (-COOH).
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the condensed formula as CH3 and COOH separately rather than a proper structural formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to draw comparative tables which include name, molecular formula, condensed formula, and structural formula of various compounds differing in functional groups.

key_points: The formula that represents the simplest ratio of various elements present in one molecule of a compound is called the empirical formula
marking_schemes.model_answer: The term defined is empirical formula — the formula representing the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the abbreviation 'EF' instead of the full term 'empirical formula'

key_points: The substance that releases hydronium ion (H3O+) as the only positive ion when dissolved in water is an acid
marking_schemes.model_answer: The term defined is acid — a substance that releases hydronium ion (H3O+) as the only positive ion when dissolved in water.
common_errors: Instead of stating the general term 'Acid', many candidates gave specific names of acids (e.g. hydrochloric acid) which were not acceptable
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Advise students to use standard abbreviations and symbols only in answering the questions.

key_points: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract electrons towards itself when combined in a covalent compound
marking_schemes.model_answer: The term defined is electronegativity — the tendency of an atom in a covalent compound to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.
common_errors: Most candidates gave the appropriate term as 'electron affinity' instead of 'electronegativity'
Some candidates wrote the abbreviation form of electronegativity
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Draw the attention of the students to the two ways in which bond pair of electrons is shared, with relevant examples.

key_points: Calcination is the process by which certain ores, especially carbonates, are converted to oxides in the absence of air
marking_schemes.model_answer: The term defined is calcination — the process of heating certain ores (especially carbonates) strongly in the absence of air to convert them to their oxides.
common_errors: A few candidates confused calcination with roasting

key_points: A non-polar covalent bond is the covalent bond in which electrons are shared equally between the combining atoms
This occurs when both atoms have the same electronegativity (e.g. H2, Cl2, O2)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The term defined is non-polar covalent bond — the covalent bond in which the electron pair is shared equally between the two combining atoms, as both have the same electronegativity.
common_errors: Many candidates incorrectly termed it as polar covalent bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Draw the attention of the students to the two ways in which bond pair of electrons is shared, with relevant examples.

key_points: Reactivity order (increasing): Pb < Zn < Ca < K
K and Ca are alkali/alkaline earth metals, highly reactive; Pb is least reactive among the four
marking_schemes.model_answer: In increasing order of reactivity: Pb, Zn, Ca, K. Lead is the least reactive and potassium is the most reactive among the four elements.
common_errors: Several candidates used greater than (>) or less than (<) symbols incorrectly
Some arranged the items in reverse order

key_points: Order of preferential discharge at cathode: Cu2+ first, then H+, then Mg2+, then Na1+
Ions lower in the electrochemical series (closer to the bottom / less reactive metals) are discharged preferentially
marking_schemes.model_answer: In the order of preferential discharge at the cathode: Cu2+, H1+, Mg2+, Na1+. Copper ions are discharged first because Cu is lowest in the activity series among the four.
common_errors: Several candidates used symbols incorrectly to arrange items

key_points: Decreasing order of ionisation potential: H > Li > Na > K
Ionisation potential decreases down a group; H has highest ionisation potential among the four
marking_schemes.model_answer: In decreasing order of ionisation potential: H, Li, Na, K. Hydrogen has the highest ionisation potential and potassium has the lowest among the four.
common_errors: Several candidates used symbols incorrectly
Some arranged the items in reverse order

key_points: Increasing order of electron affinity: B < N < O < F
Note: N has a slightly lower electron affinity than O due to its half-filled stable 2p subshell
F has the highest electron affinity among these four elements
marking_schemes.model_answer: In increasing order of electron affinity: B, N, O, F. Fluorine has the highest electron affinity; boron has the lowest. Note that nitrogen has a slightly lower electron affinity than oxygen due to its stable half-filled 2p subshell.
common_errors: Several candidates used symbols incorrectly
Some arranged the items in reverse order

key_points: Molecular weights: methane CH4 = 16; ethyne C2H2 = 26; ethene C2H4 = 28; ethane C2H6 = 30
Increasing order of molecular weight: methane (16) < ethyne (26) < ethene (28) < ethane (30)
marking_schemes.model_answer: In increasing order of molecular weight: methane (16), ethyne (26), ethene (28), ethane (30).
common_errors: Some candidates made unnecessary use of formulae instead of the names given
Some arranged the items in reverse order

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electron dot structure of N2: :N:::N: or :N≡N:
key_points: Nitrogen molecule has a triple bond between two N atoms
Each N has one lone pair (2 electrons) in the dot structure
Structure: :N≡N: (with lone pairs on each N)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The electron dot structure of nitrogen molecule (N2) shows a triple bond between the two nitrogen atoms with one lone pair on each nitrogen: :N:::N: (or :N≡N:).
common_errors: Candidates drew the orbit structure or showed electron pairs along with the bonds
Some forgot the lone pair of electrons on N
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify the difference between electron dot and orbital diagram. Emphasise that lone pairs must not be missed out.

key_points: Sodium transfers its valence electron to chlorine
Na becomes Na+ (1+) and Cl becomes Cl- (1-)
The electron dot structure should show transfer of one electron from Na to Cl and the resulting ionic charges
marking_schemes.model_answer: The electron dot diagram of sodium chloride shows sodium (Na) transferring its single valence electron to chlorine, forming Na+ and Cl-: Na• + •Cl: → Na+[Cl]-
common_errors: Electrons of sodium were not differently represented from chlorine
Transfer of electron and ion formation was not shown
A few drew the orbital diagram instead of the electron dot diagram
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to differentiate between electrons of unlike atoms. Lay emphasis on writing the positive charge on the ion.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Electron dot structure of ammonium ion (NH4+) showing coordinate bond from N to H+, overall 1+ charge
key_points: Ammonium ion (NH4+) has 4 N-H bonds: 3 covalent and 1 coordinate (dative) bond
The coordinate bond from N to H+ should be shown with an arrow
The overall charge on the ion is 1+
marking_schemes.model_answer: The electron dot diagram of the ammonium ion (NH4+) shows nitrogen bonded to four hydrogen atoms, with the fourth bond formed by donation of N's lone pair to H+ (coordinate bond shown by an arrow). The overall structure carries a 1+ charge.
common_errors: Coordinate bond was not shown by some candidates
Overall positive charge was not shown on the ion in a few cases
Some drew the structure of ammonia instead of ammonium ion
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to differentiate between electrons of unlike atoms. Lay emphasis on writing the positive charge on the ion.

key_points: A solution with pH 7 is neutral and will have no effect on litmus solution
Solution C has pH 7
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solution C (pH 7) will have no effect on litmus solution, as it is neutral.
common_errors: Some candidates failed to associate the nature of the substance with the correct pH value
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Show the association between pH scale and the nature of substances clearly to the students. Explain clearly the properties of acids and alkalis.

key_points: An acid (pH < 7) liberates CO2 when reacted with sodium carbonate
Solution B has pH 2 (acidic)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solution B (pH 2) will liberate CO2 when reacted with sodium carbonate, as it is the acidic solution.
common_errors: Some candidates attached names to solutions instead of using the symbols A, B, and C
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Show the association between pH scale and the nature of substances clearly to the students.

key_points: An alkaline solution (pH > 7) turns red litmus blue
Solution A has pH 12 (strongly alkaline)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solution A (pH 12) will turn red litmus solution blue, as it is strongly alkaline.
common_errors: Some candidates failed to associate the nature of the substance with the correct pH value
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Show the association between pH scale and the nature of substances clearly to the students.

key_points: Element B (top-left, in Group 1) forms an electrovalent (ionic) compound with G (Group 17, halogen)
Group 1 metals readily lose one electron to Group 17 non-metals
marking_schemes.model_answer: Element B forms an electrovalent (ionic) compound with G, as B is a Group 1 metal that transfers its electron to G, a Group 17 non-metal.
common_errors: Some candidates identified the elements instead of using the given letters of alphabets
The position of metals and non-metals was not clear to some candidates
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to read the questions carefully and answer as per instructions given.

key_points: Element A (positioned at top, Group 1) is a metal whose positive ion migrates towards the cathode during electrolysis
Cations (positive ions) migrate to the cathode (negative electrode)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The ion of element A (a metal forming positive ions) will migrate towards the cathode during electrolysis, as cations move to the negative electrode.
common_errors: Despite clear instructions not to repeat elements, some candidates repeated certain elements
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to read the questions carefully and answer as per instructions given.

key_points: Element E is a non-metallic element with valency 2 (Group 16 position in the periodic table extract)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Element E is the non-metallic element with a valency of 2, positioned in Group 16 of the periodic table.
common_errors: Some candidates identified elements instead of using the given letters of alphabets
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to read the questions carefully and answer as per instructions given.

key_points: Element F is an inert gas (positioned in Group 18 of the periodic table extract)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Element F is the inert gas, positioned in Group 18 of the periodic table with a completely filled valence shell.
common_errors: Some candidates identified elements instead of using the given letters
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to read the questions carefully and answer as per instructions given.

key_points: A strong electrolyte completely dissociates/ionises in solution
The particles present in a strong electrolyte solution are only ions
marking_schemes.model_answer: In a strong electrolyte, the particles present are only ions, as the compound undergoes complete dissociation/ionisation in solution.
common_errors: Some candidates listed examples instead of stating the presence of ions or molecules
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the types of electrolytes on the basis of dissociation/ionization — whether complete/partial or no dissociation/ionization.

key_points: A non-electrolyte does not dissociate into ions in solution
The particles present are only molecules
marking_schemes.model_answer: In a non-electrolyte, the particles present are only molecules, as there is no dissociation into ions.
common_errors: Some candidates listed examples instead of stating the presence of molecules
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the types of electrolytes on the basis of dissociation/ionization.

key_points: A weak electrolyte partially dissociates in solution
The particles present are both molecules (undissociated) and ions (from partial dissociation)
marking_schemes.model_answer: In a weak electrolyte, the particles present are both molecules and ions, as only partial dissociation/ionisation occurs.
common_errors: Some candidates listed examples instead of stating the presence of both ions and molecules
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the types of electrolytes on the basis of dissociation/ionization.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: On adding concentrated hydrochloric acid: if a greenish yellow gas is evolved it is Manganese dioxide. If no gas is evolved it is CuO.
key_points: Reagent: concentrated hydrochloric acid
Manganese dioxide reacts with conc. HCl to produce greenish-yellow chlorine gas: MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O
Copper(II) oxide reacts with conc. HCl to give a blue-green solution but no gas
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add concentrated hydrochloric acid to each. If a greenish-yellow gas (chlorine) is evolved, it is manganese dioxide. If no gas is evolved (only a blue-green solution forms), it is copper(II) oxide.
common_errors: Some candidates gave the equation instead of writing the observation
The result of adding the reagent to only one substance was specified without the other
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to specify the effect of the reagent on both the substances when a single test is used.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: On adding sodium hydroxide solution: if a dirty green precipitate is formed it is ferrous sulphate solution. If a reddish-brown precipitate is formed, it is ferric sulphate solution.
key_points: Reagent: sodium hydroxide solution
Ferrous sulphate (FeSO4) + NaOH → dirty green precipitate of Fe(OH)2
Ferric sulphate (Fe2(SO4)3) + NaOH → reddish-brown precipitate of Fe(OH)3
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add sodium hydroxide solution to each. If a dirty green precipitate forms, it is ferrous sulphate solution [Fe(OH)2]. If a reddish-brown precipitate forms, it is ferric sulphate solution [Fe(OH)3].
common_errors: Some candidates interchanged the colours of the two ions (ferrous and ferric)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Supplement theory adequately with practical work. Instruct students to record observations.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: On adding lead nitrate solution: if white precipitate formed dissolves on heating it is dilute HCl. If white precipitate formed does not dissolve on heating it is dilute H2SO4.
key_points: Reagent: lead nitrate solution
Both dilute HCl and dilute H2SO4 form white precipitates with lead nitrate (PbCl2 and PbSO4 respectively)
PbCl2 is soluble in hot water (dissolves on heating); PbSO4 is insoluble in hot water (does not dissolve on heating)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Add lead nitrate solution to each. Both form a white precipitate. On heating: if the white precipitate dissolves, it is dilute HCl (PbCl2 is soluble in hot water). If the white precipitate does not dissolve on heating, it is dilute H2SO4 (PbSO4 is insoluble).
common_errors: White precipitate was mentioned by several candidates but the effect of heat on both was not mentioned
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to specify the effect of the reagent on both the substances when a single test is used.

key_points: Lead chloride (PbCl2) is insoluble and is prepared by the precipitation method
e.g. Pb(NO3)2 + 2NaCl → PbCl2↓ + 2NaNO3
marking_schemes.model_answer: Lead chloride is prepared by the method of precipitation (B), since PbCl2 is insoluble and forms a precipitate when soluble lead salt is mixed with a soluble chloride.
common_errors: Several candidates incorrectly chose neutralization instead of precipitation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to specify the effect of the reagent on both the substances when a single test is used. Never disregard the importance of practical work.

key_points: Iron(II) sulphate (FeSO4) is prepared by the substitution (displacement) method
e.g. Fe + H2SO4(dil.) → FeSO4 + H2 (iron displaces hydrogen from dilute sulphuric acid)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Iron(II) sulphate is prepared by the substitution (displacement) method (D): iron displaces hydrogen from dilute sulphuric acid: Fe + H2SO4(dil.) → FeSO4 + H2.
common_errors: Some candidates erred by writing precipitation instead of substitution

key_points: Sodium nitrate (NaNO3) is prepared by neutralization
e.g. NaOH + HNO3 → NaNO3 + H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: Sodium nitrate is prepared by the neutralization method (A): NaOH + HNO3 → NaNO3 + H2O.
common_errors: This subpart of the question was attempted correctly by most candidates

key_points: Iron(III) chloride (FeCl3) is prepared by direct combination (synthesis)
2Fe + 3Cl2 → 2FeCl3 (iron heated in excess chlorine)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Iron(III) chloride is prepared by direct combination (C): 2Fe + 3Cl2 → 2FeCl3 (heated iron in excess chlorine).
common_errors: Most candidates attempted this subpart correctly

key_points: Sulphur is oxidised by concentrated nitric acid to sulphuric acid
Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is produced
Balanced equation: S + 6HNO3(conc.) → H2SO4 + 6NO2 + 2H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: The balanced equation for sulphur reacting with concentrated nitric acid is: S + 6HNO3(conc.) → H2SO4 + 6NO2 + 2H2O.
common_errors: A large number of candidates made errors in balancing the equation
Many candidates wrote SO2 as a product instead of H2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

key_points: Carbon is oxidised by concentrated sulphuric acid to carbon dioxide
Sulphuric acid is reduced to sulphur dioxide
Balanced equation: C + 2H2SO4(conc.) → CO2 + 2SO2 + 2H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: The balanced equation for carbon reacting with concentrated sulphuric acid is: C + 2H2SO4(conc.) → CO2 + 2SO2 + 2H2O.
common_errors: Although CO2 was the correct product, several candidates wrote H2CO3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

key_points: Copper reacts with dilute nitric acid to form copper nitrate, nitric oxide (NO), and water
Balanced equation: 3Cu + 8HNO3(dil.) → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: The balanced equation for copper reacting with dilute nitric acid is: 3Cu + 8HNO3(dil.) → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO↑ + 4H2O.
common_errors: Many candidates wrote NO2 as a product instead of NO (NO2 is produced with concentrated HNO3)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions. Use of structural formulae for organic compounds will help students write equations correctly.

key_points: Ethene is prepared from bromoethane (C2H5Br) by dehydrohalogenation using alcoholic KOH
Balanced equation: C2H5Br + KOH(alc.) → C2H4 + KBr + H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ethene is prepared from bromoethane by reaction with alcoholic KOH (dehydrohalogenation): C2H5Br + KOH(alc.) → C2H4 + KBr + H2O.
common_errors: The formula for bromoethane was written as C2H6Br in place of C2H5Br by some candidates
Several candidates used chloroethane instead of bromoethane
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

key_points: Ethyne (acetylene) is prepared by the action of water on calcium carbide
Balanced equation: CaC2 + 2H2O → C2H2 + Ca(OH)2
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ethyne is prepared from calcium carbide by reaction with water: CaC2 + 2H2O → C2H2↑ + Ca(OH)2.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote the product as CaO instead of Ca(OH)2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to prepare a chart on various homologous series with the first member listed along with other properties.

key_points: Methane is prepared from sodium acetate (sodium ethanoate) by reaction with NaOH (soda-lime), heated
Balanced equation: CH3COONa + NaOH → CH4 + Na2CO3
marking_schemes.model_answer: Methane is prepared by heating sodium acetate with sodium hydroxide: CH3COONa + NaOH → CH4↑ + Na2CO3.
common_errors: The formula of sodium acetate was written incorrectly by some candidates
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give adequate practice in writing balanced chemical equations with necessary conditions.

key_points: A compound with 3 carbon atoms and a carboxyl (-COOH) functional group is propanoic acid
Formula: CH3CH2COOH; IUPAC name: propanoic acid
marking_schemes.model_answer: The organic compound with 3 carbon atoms and a carboxyl functional group is propanoic acid (CH3CH2COOH).
common_errors: Some candidates incorrectly drew the structural formula when the name of the organic compound was asked
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that students know the common names along with the IUPAC names, wherever possible.

key_points: The general formula CnH2n represents alkenes
The first member (n=2) of the alkene series is ethene (C2H4)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The first homologue of the general formula CnH2n is ethene (C2H4), also called ethylene.
common_errors: Several candidates gave incorrect answers like alkene, ethyne, or acetylene
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to prepare a chart on various homologous series with the first member listed along with other properties.

key_points: The compound that reacts with acetic acid (ethanoic acid) to form ethyl ethanoate (ethyl acetate) is ethanol
CH3COOH + C2H5OH → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (esterification)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The compound that reacts with acetic acid to form ethyl ethanoate is ethanol (ethyl alcohol, C2H5OH): CH3COOH + C2H5OH → CH3COOC2H5 + H2O.
common_errors: Reactants listed by many candidates for this reaction were incorrect
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that students know the common names along with the IUPAC names, wherever possible.

key_points: Complete chlorination of ethyne (C2H2) adds 4 chlorine atoms
Product: 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane (C2H2Cl4)
C2H2 + 2Cl2 → C2H2Cl4 (1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The compound formed by complete chlorination of ethyne is 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane (C2H2Cl4): C2H2 + 2Cl2 → CHCl2-CHCl2.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote incorrect numbering of the C atoms having the chlorine atoms
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ask students to prepare a chart on various homologous series. Ensure that students know the common names along with the IUPAC names.

key_points: Chemical formula of Bauxite is Al2O3.2H2O (hydrated aluminium oxide)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The chemical formula of Bauxite is Al2O3.2H2O.
common_errors: Many candidates either wrote incorrect number of water molecules or did not write water of crystallisation at all
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Frequently revise names of common ores of aluminium, iron, and zinc.

key_points: Chemical formula of Cryolite is Na3AlF6 (sodium hexafluoroaluminate)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The chemical formula of Cryolite is Na3AlF6.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote incorrect formulae for cryolite
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Frequently revise names of common ores of aluminium, iron, and zinc.

key_points: Chemical formula of Sodium aluminate is NaAlO2
marking_schemes.model_answer: The chemical formula of Sodium aluminate is NaAlO2.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote incorrect formulae for sodium aluminate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Frequently revise names of common ores of aluminium, iron, and zinc.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cryolite reduces the fusion temperature of the mixture / increases the mobility of ions / increases the conductivity of the electrolyte / acts as solvent for alumina.
key_points: Cryolite lowers the fusion (melting) temperature of alumina from ~2050°C to ~950°C
It increases ionic mobility and conductivity of the electrolyte
It acts as a solvent for alumina
marking_schemes.model_answer: In the Hall-Heroult Process, cryolite is used because it reduces the fusion temperature of the alumina mixture, increases the mobility of ions, and increases the electrical conductivity of the electrolyte, acting as a solvent for alumina.
accepted_alternatives: Cryolite increases the conductivity of the electrolyte
common_errors: Most candidates answered this question correctly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the questions based on the extraction of aluminium from alumina by Hall-Heroult's process in class.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Powdered coke protects the graphite rods of the anode from oxidation by oxygen released at the anode / prevents the loss of heat from the electrolyte.
key_points: Powdered coke (carbon) is sprinkled on top to protect the graphite anode rods from oxidation by oxygen evolved at the anode
It also acts as a heat insulator, reducing heat loss from the molten electrolyte
marking_schemes.model_answer: Powdered coke is sprinkled on top of the electrolyte to protect the graphite anode rods from oxidation by the oxygen gas released at the anode, and to prevent heat loss from the electrolyte.
accepted_alternatives: Prevents loss of heat from the electrolyte
common_errors: Most candidates answered this question correctly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the questions based on the extraction of aluminium from alumina by Hall-Heroult's process in class.

key_points: During the Hall-Heroult Process, aluminium is collected at the cathode (negative electrode)
Al3+ + 3e- → Al (reduction at cathode)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Aluminium is collected from the cathode during the electrolysis of alumina in the Hall-Heroult Process, as Al3+ ions are reduced at the cathode.
common_errors: Most candidates answered this question correctly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the questions based on the extraction of aluminium from alumina by Hall-Heroult's process in class.

key_points: Duralumin is used for making aircraft bodies due to its lightness and strength
marking_schemes.model_answer: Duralumin is matched to C — Aircraft body. Its combination of low weight and high strength makes it ideal for aircraft construction.
common_errors: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II, not being sure of the uses of alloys
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students metallurgy in detail. Familiarise students with the role of each metal used in an alloy.

key_points: Solder (an alloy of lead and tin) has a low melting point and is used for electrical fuses and joining electrical connections
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solder is matched to A — Electrical fuse. Its low melting point makes it suitable for use in electrical fuses and joining wires.
common_errors: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students metallurgy in detail.

key_points: Brass (an alloy of copper and zinc) is used for decorative articles, musical instruments, and fittings
marking_schemes.model_answer: Brass is matched to D — Decorative articles. Brass has an attractive golden appearance and good workability, making it suitable for decorative uses.
common_errors: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students metallurgy in detail.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Stainless Steel: B or Surgical instruments
key_points: Stainless steel (alloy of iron, carbon, chromium, nickel) is corrosion-resistant and used for surgical instruments
marking_schemes.model_answer: Stainless Steel is matched to B — Surgical instruments. Its corrosion resistance and strength make it ideal for medical and surgical tools.
common_errors: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students metallurgy in detail.

key_points: The catalyst used to oxidise ammonia (in Ostwald's Process for nitric acid manufacture) is platinum (Pt)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The catalyst used to oxidise ammonia is platinum (Pt). In Ostwald's Process, ammonia is oxidised to nitric oxide over a platinum catalyst: 4NH3 + 5O2 → 4NO + 6H2O.
common_errors: A few candidates mentioned incorrect catalysts such as Fe, V2O5, or CaO
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Maintain a comparative chart for various processes consisting of reactants, catalysts, temperature/pressure condition, equation, etc.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Acetic acid or ethanoic acid or CH3COOH
key_points: Acetic acid (ethanoic acid, CH3COOH) has a vinegar-like smell
When solidified, it forms a glacial (ice-like) mass — hence called glacial acetic acid
marking_schemes.model_answer: The organic compound that when solidified forms an ice-like mass is acetic acid (ethanoic acid, CH3COOH). In its pure solidified form it is called glacial acetic acid.
common_errors: Almost all candidates answered correctly

key_points: Dilute nitric acid (HNO3) is an oxidising acid — it acts as an oxidising agent in both dilute and concentrated forms
HCl and H2SO4 are not typically oxidising acids in dilute form
marking_schemes.model_answer: The dilute acid that is an oxidising agent is nitric acid (HNO3). Unlike HCl and H2SO4, dilute HNO3 acts as an oxidising agent.
common_errors: Many candidates listed HCl or H2SO4 as an oxidising agent instead of nitric acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Teach students the fact that only nitric acid in dilute and concentrated form can act as an oxidizing agent.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: RMW of NaOH = 40, Cu(OH)2 = 98; 2 × 40 g precipitate = 98 g; 200 g precipitate = (98 × 200)/80 = 245 g
key_points: From equation: 2NaOH + CuSO4 → Na2SO4 + Cu(OH)2
2 moles NaOH (2 × 40 = 80 g) produces 1 mole Cu(OH)2 (= 98 g)
200 g NaOH produces (98 × 200)/80 = 245 g of Cu(OH)2
marking_schemes.model_answer: From the equation, 2 × 40 = 80 g of NaOH produces 98 g of Cu(OH)2. Therefore 200 g of NaOH produces (98 × 200)/80 = 245 g of copper hydroxide.
common_errors: Some candidates used Gay Lussac's law instead of the mole concept
Some calculated the molecular mass incorrectly
Some failed to use the stoichiometric coefficient of 2 for NaOH
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to answer the molar relationship using the coefficients in the equation and compute the answer accurately. Insist on stepwise working of numerical problems.

key_points: The precipitate of copper hydroxide Cu(OH)2 is pale blue in colour
marking_schemes.model_answer: The colour of the copper hydroxide precipitate formed is pale blue.
common_errors: Some candidates incorrectly wrote the colour of the precipitate as brown or white
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instruct students to focus on practical work and the noting of results.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: Empirical formula C5H5N; Empirical formula weight = 79; n = (2 × 39.5)/79 = 1; Molecular formula = C5H5N
key_points: Divide by smallest (1.268): C = 5, H = 5, N = 1
Empirical formula: C5H5N; empirical formula weight = (5×12) + (5×1) + 14 = 79
Molecular weight = 2 × vapour density = 2 × 39.5 = 79
n = molecular weight / empirical formula weight = 79/79 = 1
Molecular formula = C5H5N (same as empirical formula)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dividing percentage by atomic mass: C = 75.92/12 = 6.32; H = 6.32/1 = 6.32; N = 17.76/14 = 1.268. Dividing by the smallest (1.268): C:H:N = 5:5:1. Empirical formula: C5H5N. Empirical formula weight = 60 + 5 + 14 = 79. Molecular weight = 2 × 39.5 = 79. n = 79/79 = 1. Molecular formula = C5H5N.
common_errors: Many candidates determined the empirical formula correctly but failed in calculating the value of n and hence erred in the molecular formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to answer the molar relationship using the coefficients in the equation. Insist on stepwise working of numerical problems and give adequate practice.

key_points: During electrolytic reduction of alumina (Al2O3), the gas evolved at the anode is oxygen (O2)
Anode reaction: 2O2- → O2 + 4e-
marking_schemes.model_answer: When alumina undergoes electrolytic reduction (in the Hall-Heroult Process), oxygen gas (O2) is evolved at the anode.
common_errors: Some candidates wrote CO2 instead of O2
A few wrote the symbol of nascent oxygen (O) which was not acceptable
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to learn the reactions in terms of reactants, products, conditions, equations, and observations.

key_points: When ethene undergoes hydrogenation, hydrogen adds across the double bond to form ethane
C2H4 + H2 → C2H6 (ethane)
marking_schemes.model_answer: When ethene undergoes hydrogenation, ethane gas (C2H6) is produced: C2H4 + H2 → C2H6.
common_errors: Several candidates wrote H2 is evolved in the hydrogenation reaction of ethene (incorrect — H2 is a reactant, not a product)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Give enough practice to students in writing the different types of balanced chemical reactions.

key_points: When ammonia reacts with heated copper oxide, the gases/products formed include nitrogen (N2) as the gaseous product from ammonia
2NH3 + 3CuO → N2 + 3Cu + 3H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: When ammonia reacts with heated copper oxide, the gas evolved is nitrogen (N2): 2NH3 + 3CuO → N2 + 3Cu + 3H2O.
common_errors: The gas evolved was incorrectly written as N, NO, or NO2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Train students to learn the reactions in terms of reactants, products, conditions, equations, and observations.

key_points: Reaction A: Magnesium nitride reacts with water to produce magnesium hydroxide and ammonia
Balanced equation: Mg3N2 + 6H2O → 3Mg(OH)2 + 2NH3
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reaction A: Mg3N2 + 6H2O → 3Mg(OH)2 + 2NH3. Magnesium nitride reacts with warm water to give magnesium hydroxide and ammonia gas.
common_errors: MgO was written as the product instead of Mg(OH)2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students that a metal nitride with warm water gives metal hydroxide and ammonia.

key_points: Reaction B: Ammonia reacts with hydrochloric acid to form ammonium chloride
NH3 + HCl → NH4Cl
Alternatively, ammonia in excess with chlorine: 8NH3 + 3Cl2 → 6NH4Cl + N2
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reaction B: NH3 + HCl → NH4Cl. Ammonia combines with hydrogen chloride gas to form ammonium chloride (white fumes).
common_errors: Most candidates gave correct balanced equations for this reaction
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students that ammonium salts react with an alkali and give NH3 gas.

marking_schemes.scheme_text: NH4Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH3 + H2O or with any other alkali
key_points: Reaction C: Ammonium chloride reacts with an alkali (e.g. NaOH) to produce ammonia gas
NH4Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH3 + H2O
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reaction C: NH4Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH3↑ + H2O. Ammonium chloride reacts with sodium hydroxide (or any other alkali) to liberate ammonia gas.
accepted_alternatives: NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 → CaCl2 + 2NH3 + 2H2O (or any other alkali)
common_errors: Some candidates failed to use an alkali for reaction C
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students that ammonium salts react with an alkali and give NH3 gas.

key_points: The industrial method for the preparation of ammonia is the Haber's Process (Haber-Bosch Process)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The industrial method for the preparation of ammonia is Haber's Process.
common_errors: Name of the process was incorrectly written as Ostwald's process or Baeyer's process
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify industrial methods for the preparation of ammonia and sulphuric acid thoroughly.

key_points: The catalytic equation for Haber's Process: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 with iron (Fe) as catalyst
Conditions: high temperature (~450°C), high pressure (~200 atm)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The catalytic equation for the Haber's Process is: N2 + 3H2 → (Fe catalyst, ~450°C, ~200 atm) 2NH3.
common_errors: The catalyst listed was incorrectly given as platinum or nickel (iron is the correct catalyst)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify industrial methods for the preparation of ammonia and sulphuric acid thoroughly.

key_points: The industrial method for the preparation of sulphuric acid is the Contact Process
marking_schemes.model_answer: The industrial method for the preparation of sulphuric acid is the Contact Process.
common_errors: Haber's Process was incorrectly written instead of Contact Process
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify industrial methods for the preparation of ammonia and sulphuric acid thoroughly.

key_points: Key reaction in the Contact Process: oxidation of SO2 to SO3 using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) catalyst
Balanced equation: 2SO2 + O2 → 2SO3 (with V2O5 or Pt as catalyst)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The catalytic equation for the Contact Process: 2SO2 + O2 → (V2O5 catalyst) 2SO3. Vanadium pentoxide (or platinum) is used as the catalyst.
common_errors: Incorrect equation was given by some candidates
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify industrial methods for the preparation of ammonia and sulphuric acid thoroughly.
